note: The artifact the raft-rs-wasm backend loads, how it was built, and the raft-rs 0.7 sources the host contract is cited against. Integrity is required; reproducibility is measured and reported as found.

reproducibility.observation: the generated JavaScript glue is byte-identical across builds of one source (attempts 1 to 4 share one glue; attempts 5 and 6 share the glue that adds the step_down_removed_leader export); the .wasm is not. For attempts 5 and 6 the difference was read: wasm-bindgen 0.2.104 emits three of its cast imports in a different order per run. Reported as measured; byte-for-byte reproducibility is not assumed.
reproducibility.note: attempts 1 and 2 measured reproducibility of the original source; attempt 3 recorded the three-fix intermediate build; attempt 4 recorded the four-fix build; attempts 5 and 6 measured reproducibility of the five-fix source, and attempt 5 is the current checked-in artifact after all five fork fixes.

forkFixes.fix: with_node takes the node out of the handle table for the duration of the call
forkFixes.why: a raft-rs fatal! inside the closure left the NODES RefCell borrowed for ever (panic=abort on wasm32, so no unwinding and no catch_unwind); every later call on EVERY handle then trapped "RefCell already borrowed", including create_node and free. Measured before and after.

forkFixes.fix: decode_conf_change_entry returns an error on undecodable base64
forkFixes.why: upstream unwrap_or_default() turned corrupt data into an EMPTY change list, which is a valid request to leave a joint configuration

forkFixes.fix: pending_conf_index crosses as a decimal string
forkFixes.why: it was the one u64 crossing as a JS number

forkFixes.fix: every recoverable binding refusal crosses as a tagged object
forkFixes.why: the private invocation owner must distinguish CORE_REFUSED from a WASM trap by construction, without inspecting a generic JavaScript exception class or message

forkFixes.fix: step_down_removed_leader: a leader its own applied configuration removed becomes a follower at its current term
forkFixes.why: raft-rs leaves a leader that applied its own removal leading (raft.rs post_conf_change: "TODO(tbg): step down (for sanity)") with no Progress for itself: it drops every proposal, its heartbeats keep the remaining voters from electing, and maybe_commit and on_persist_entries unwrap the Progress it no longer has, which aborts the module. RawNode gives the host no way to end that leadership (MsgCheckQuorum is refused as a local message; a node that is not promotable cannot campaign). The function calls the crate's public become_follower(term, INVALID_ID) - the transition its own check-quorum makes - only for a leader that is not promotable and holds no Progress for itself, and answers a tagged refusal naming the state, changing nothing, in every other state.

vendoredAt: vendor/raft-rs-wasm — generated and vendored infrastructure for the production raft-rs-wasm consensus backend loaded by src/raft/raft-rs-binding-owner.js. It lives outside src/ because wasm-pack output is nobody's handwritten JavaScript source: keeping it out of the source tree lets every repository checker stay on its own default walk with no exclusion for it, while package.json files ships it.

citationSources.note: The raft-rs 0.7.0 sources the host contract cites, vendored so a citation resolves without a cargo registry. The chain is: the crates.io checksum recorded as raftCrateChecksum is the sha256 of the published .crate tarball; these files were extracted from that tarball and their own digests recorded here.
